note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a IRE 15; A06b IRE 15; L05 IRE 19(1)(e)): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another (loss applies only to naturalised citizens, not modelled). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: Parental residence restriction) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. Naturalisation costs an adult €175 to apply and €950 for the certificate once approved, €1,125 in all; most applications are processed within 12 months (Immigration Service Delivery, read 30 October 2026; the 12 months are the usual time, not a legal maximum). ISD's requirements name no language or civics test, so none is held.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Ireland, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Ireland for 5 out of the last 9 years, including the year preceding the application. Intention to continue to reside in Ireland required. ... n.a. ... Person voluntarily acquires citizenship of another country otherwise than by marriage and acquired Irish citizenship by naturalisation. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Ireland to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a citizen who was born on the island of Ireland; Person and parent are both born outside the island of Ireland, unless the parent is abroad in public service ... Parental residence restriction ... Person is born in Ireland to a citizen, or to a person with permanent residence in Ireland or the UK, or to a person who was resident in Ireland for 3 out of the last 4 years. ... No provision

sources.title: Immigration Service Delivery (Department of Justice), Become an Irish citizen by naturalisation
sources.said: The application fee for each application for naturalisation is €175 ... Most applications for citizenship by naturalisation are processed within 12 months ... €950 – Adult

atBirth.soilIf: Person is born in Ireland to a citizen, or to a person with permanent residence in Ireland or the UK, or to a person who was resident in Ireland for 3 out of the last 4 years.
